title: upgrade-shepherd-preflight-hypothesis
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a modular preflight harness ("Upgrade Shepherd") that runs a layered set of validation checks prior to upgrade rollouts. The harness must be LTS-aware (selects narrow compatibility checks for LTS lines), support both canary and staged rollouts, and provide deterministic pass/fail signals for: smoke tests, latency P95/P99 regression gates, token-per-cost delta, and a small eval suite of prompt-level correctness checks. The goal is to reduce manual upgrade time and surface regressions early while keeping false positives low.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible pipeline (k8s Job/Argo workflow) that runs preflight for a candidate runtime build and emits a single JSON verdict with structured reasons
Perf gates defined: latency P95 and P99 thresholds per model family and sequence length bucket; automatic tolerance scaling for canary size
Smoke tests that cover: service boot, model load, KV cache warmup, prefix-cache correctness, and graceful fallback behavior
Small eval suite (<= 50 prompts) with golden answers and fuzzy-match thresholds for top-level regressions
Integration with Console: per-run artifact links, a pass/fail badge on the release page, and tokenized cost delta estimates
Automation for aborting rollouts on high-severity failures and creating a rollback task in Linear
notes: We want the harness to be extensible so QA and platform engineers can add evaluation suites without changing core logic. For LTS lines we run an additional compatibility probe set that exercises pinned quantization kernels and older KV cache behavior. Canary sizing heuristics should be based on recent production traffic percentiles (default: 0.1% of traffic for small canaries).
implementation_steps: Design prototype workflow and verdict schema (JSON with reasons and metric deltas)
Implement modular test runners: smoke-runner, perf-runner, eval-runner
Add LTS-aware probe selector service (simple config map lookup initially)
Wire tests into CI/CD: release pipeline triggers preflight artifact run
Integrate verdicts into Console and create rollback automation
Run 3 full preflight cycles on runtime-1.20 -> runtime-1.21 dry runs and iterate thresholds
risks_and_tradeoffs: Tight perf thresholds increase false positives which delay rollouts — mitigated by a staged threshold ramp and manual overrides
Long-running eval suites slow down preflight — keep eval suites small and allow a full regression job asynchronously
Adding too many probes increases maintenance; prioritize coverage for components most likely to regress (kernel changes, cache logic, batching)
implementation_notes: Prefer keeping test artifacts (traces, sample responses, golden diffs) in an artifacts bucket for 30 days to aid debugging. Use synthetic workload fabric from ENG-62321 to simulate production-like request mixes. For perf measurements prefer stable windowed sampling (5m) and compare to baseline snapshots stored per-build.
comments: 2025-02-18 — Aisha Kapoor: Initial write-up and hypothesis. Put together a minimal acceptance criteria list and suggested thresholds for P95/P99 based on historical telemetry. Recommended starting thresholds: P95 <= baseline*1.25, P99 <= baseline*1.4 for canary runs (configurable).

2025-02-21 — Jonah Lee: Split into three modular runners and drafted the verdict schema. Prototype verdict JSON includes 'status', 'reasons', 'metric_deltas', 'baseline_snapshot_id'. Posting PRs for review.

2025-02-25 — Priya Menon (QA): Added 40 curated prompts for eval-runner targeting hallucination regressions and function-call formatting. Proposed fuzzy-match rules with edit-distance and embedding similarity.

2025-02-28 — Marco Delgado (SRE): Note about running preflight in a dedicated namespace with resource quotas and node affinity to avoid noisy neighbor interference. Also flagged the need for cost cap alerts during long perf runs.

2025-03-03 — Jonah Lee: Ran first dry preflight against runtime-1.21-rc1. Perf-runner surfaced a 22% P99 increase on long-seq kernels for one model family; smoke-runner passed. Logged detailed artifact at grafana link and opened runtime PR for kernel fallback.
